reading.body:
CyrusOne Totowa holds 6 MW of IT capacity in a 200,000 square-foot facility in northern New Jersey, translating to roughly 150 racks at typical AI training density.

This facility ranks fourth among the five New Jersey data centers with published power specs, accounting for 5.4% of the state's announced 111.3 MW of IT capacity. New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities total, but only five disclose power in published operator specifications. The disclosed base is sparse enough that individual facility capacity becomes meaningful to track.

The site sits in the densest data center region in the United States, where power access and grid headroom are heavily contested resources. Six megawatts is modest against hyperscale standards, yet it represents material demand on a grid already strained by regional concentration. The lack of disclosure from 43 of 48 New Jersey facilities means announced capacity substantially understates actual power draw, and therefore actual constraint on the grid.
